provenance: SYNTHETIC -- fabricated engineering constraints. Ranges grounded in published femoral bone-plate literature and orthopaedic biomechanics. Surgical planning (segmentation, screw placement, load estimation) is a declared PRE-SOLVED input for this project. Not patient data. No clinical, FDA, ISO or ASTM claim.

material.name: Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5), annealed
material.allowable_basis: yield 880 MPa with a safety factor of 2.5 => 352 MPa, rounded down to 350

load_cases.basis: single-leg stance, ~3x bodyweight for a 70 kg patient

protected weight-bearing during early healing, ~47% of the ~15 Nm peak diaphyseal bending moment of unrestricted level gait. A plated femur is not walked on unrestricted: partial weight-bearing is the standard post-operative protocol while the fracture consolidates, and the plate is sized for that period. Applied to the plate alone, with no load sharing with the bone -- conservative for a plate bridging a fracture gap.
load_cases.axis_note: The moment vector is medio-lateral, so bending occurs in the sagittal plane. validators/stress.py computes both bending planes and reports the worse, because this frame calls +X both lateral (case, generator) and anterior (make_bone bow), and those cannot both be true.

threshold_notes.min_bone_gap_mm: Lower bound on the plate-bone gap. Pressing a plate onto bone crushes the periosteum and interrupts the blood supply the fracture heals through, so zero clearance is a failure and not an optimum. This is why limited-contact plate designs exist.
threshold_notes.max_keepout_encroach_mm: Renamed from max_keepout_violation_mm3: the check measures a linear encroachment in mm, not a volume in mm^3, and the old name never matched the units.
threshold_notes.enforced: max_stress_MPa is enforced: validators/stress.py measures section properties off the exported solid (autoimplants/section.py) and applies load_cases, so load_cases is live. See the enforced-checks table in DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md section 6.
threshold_notes.unenforced: min_screw_pullout_N is read only to populate a limit. Pull-out depends on bone quality and screw geometry, both locked surgical planning inputs -- no change to the plate can move it, so screw_pullout_min reports SKIP rather than a number that could never drive the loop.

design_space_note: READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING ANY THRESHOLD. The constraints above are chosen so that no combination of scalar parameter tweaks can pass, and that property is now measured rather than asserted -- validators/stress.py runs beam theory over cross-sections read off the exported solid. Three numbers define the window, all swept over the full legal space (width to the 17.6 mm keepout limit, thickness to the 5.6 mm the 6.0 mm standoff cap allows, mass to 55 g): the baseline 180 x 16 x 3.0 mm plate peaks at 914 MPa; the best CONSTANT-thickness design anywhere in that space still fails at 396 MPa, 13% over the 350 MPa allowable; a variable-thickness design within the same 55 g passes at 316 MPa. So scalar tuning cannot close it and redistributing material can, which is exactly the intended lesson. The window is narrow: at 50 g even a variable-thickness design fails, and at 60 g a plain constant-thickness plate passes outright and the argument collapses. The mass cap and the gait moment are therefore a matched pair -- change one and re-run the sweep. Widening is blocked by the perforating_vessel_bundle keepout at 17.6 mm (zone centre y=14.8 mm minus its 6.0 mm radius). Lengthening is blocked by the proximal and distal keepouts. What is left is contouring the plate to the bone (fixes conformance) and redistributing section toward the peak moment (fixes stress). HISTORY: this note previously argued from a 412 MPa figure produced by validators/stub.py while the real stress validator returned SKIP. Measured honestly at the old 39 g / 15 Nm thresholds, the lightest design meeting 350 MPa weighed 92 g -- the case was infeasible and no design could have passed.
